units.zh: 契丹者，古匈奴之種也。
units.en: The Khitan were descended from the ancient Xiongnu.
units.literal: The Khitan are the stock of the ancient Xiongnu.

units.zh: 代居遼澤之中，潢水南岸，南距榆關一千一百里，榆關南距幽州七百里，本鮮卑之舊地也。
units.en: For generations they lived in the Liao marshes on the south bank of the Huang River. Yuguan lay eleven hundred li to their south, and Youzhou another seven hundred li beyond the pass — lands that had once belonged to the Xianbei.
units.literal: For generations they dwelt amid the Liao marshes, on the south bank of the Huang River; one thousand one hundred li south to Yuguan, and seven hundred li south from Yuguan to Youzhou — the old territory of the Xianbei.

units.zh: 其風土人物，世代君長，前史載之詳矣。
units.en: Earlier histories already describe their land and customs, their people, and the succession of their chieftains at length.
units.literal: Their customs, land, and people, and their successive chieftains, earlier histories record in detail.

units.zh: 唐咸通末，其王曰習爾之，疆土稍大，累來朝貢。
units.en: Late in Tang's Xiantong reign, their king was Xierzhi. His domain expanded modestly, and he sent tribute to the Tang court on several occasions.
units.literal: At the end of the Xiantong era of Tang, their king was called Xierzhi; his territory grew somewhat, and he repeatedly came to court with tribute.

units.zh: 光啟中，其王欽德者，乘中原多故，北邊無備，遂蠶食諸郡，達靼、奚、室韋之屬，咸被驅役，族帳浸盛，有時入寇。
units.en: During Guangqi, King Qinde exploited turmoil in the Central Plains and the undefended northern border to swallow neighboring prefectures one by one. He subjugated the Tatars, Xi, Shiwei, and kindred peoples, his tribal encampments grew ever stronger, and his horsemen raided the frontier from time to time.
units.literal: In the Guangqi era, their king Qinde, taking advantage of many troubles in the Central Plains and no defenses on the northern frontier, then nibbled away at the commanderies; the Tatars, Xi, Shiwei, and the like were all driven to service, clan tents gradually flourished, and at times they raided in.

units.zh: 劉仁恭鎮幽州，素知契丹軍情偽，選將練兵，乘秋深入，逾摘星嶺討之，霜降秋暮，即燔塞下野草以困之，馬多饑死，即以良馬賂仁恭，以市牧地。
units.en: Liu Rengong, military governor of Youzhou, knew the Khitan forces well. He picked able commanders, drilled his troops, and each autumn drove deep beyond Zhaxing Ridge to strike them. When the first frost came, he burned the grass along the border to deny their herds forage, and many Khitan horses starved. The Khitan then sent fine horses as gifts to buy grazing rights from him.
units.literal: Liu Rengong governed Youzhou and had long known the Khitan army's strengths and deceits; he chose generals and trained troops, took advantage of autumn to penetrate deep, crossed Zhaxing Ridge to attack them, and when frost fell at autumn's end he burned the grass below the passes to distress them — many horses starved to death — whereupon they presented fine horses to bribe Rengong and buy pasturage.

units.zh: 仁恭季年荒恣，出居大安山，契丹背盟，數來寇鈔。
units.en: In his later years Rengong grew reckless and extravagant and withdrew to Great Peace Mountain. The Khitan broke their treaty and raided the frontier again and again.
units.literal: In Rengong's late years he was dissolute and extravagant, went out to dwell on Great Peace Mountain, the Khitan broke the alliance, and repeatedly came to raid and plunder.

units.zh: 時劉守光戍平州，契丹實裏王子率萬騎攻之，守光偽與之和，張幄幕於城外以享之，部族就席，伏甲起，擒實裏王子入城。
units.en: Liu Shouguang was then defending Pingzhou when the Khitan Prince Shili attacked with ten thousand horsemen. Shouguang pretended to sue for peace and set up feast tents outside the walls. When the Khitan clansmen had taken their seats, his hidden troops sprang up, seized Prince Shili, and hauled him into the city.
units.literal: At that time Liu Shouguang garrisoned Pingzhou; the Khitan Prince Shili led ten thousand horsemen to attack him. Shouguang feigned peace, spread pavilions outside the city to feast them, the tribes took their seats, hidden armor rose up, and they seized Prince Shili and brought him into the city.

units.zh: 部族聚哭，請納馬五千以贖之，不許，欽德乞盟納賂以求之，自是十餘年不能犯塞。
units.en: The clans assembled in mourning and offered five thousand horses as ransom, but Shouguang refused. Qinde sued for peace and paid a heavy price to win the prince back. For more than ten years afterward the Khitan did not breach the border.
units.literal: The tribes gathered and wept, asked to offer five thousand horses to ransom him — not permitted — Qinde begged alliance and offered bribes to obtain his release; from then on for more than ten years they could not violate the frontier.

units.zh: 及欽德政衰，有別部長耶律阿保機，最推雄勁，族帳漸盛，遂代欽德為主。
units.en: As Qinde's power waned, a leader of another branch, Yelü Abaoji, rose as the strongest man among them. His following grew until he supplanted Qinde as chief.
units.literal: When Qinde's rule declined, there was a chief of another division, Yelü Abaoji, most acclaimed for fierce strength; clan tents gradually flourished, and he then replaced Qinde as lord.

units.zh: 先是，契丹之先大賀氏有勝兵四萬，分為八部，每部皆號大人，內推一人為主，建旗鼓以尊之，每三年第其名以代之。
units.en: Long before, the Khitan Dahe clan had mustered forty thousand fighting men in eight divisions. Each division had its own Great Man, and the tribes would choose one leader among them, raise his banner and drums, and rotate the office every three years by ranked succession.
units.literal: Earlier, among the Khitan forebears the Dahe clan had forty thousand fit warriors, divided into eight divisions; each division was titled Great Man, and within they chose one man as lord, raised flags and drums to honor him, and every three years ranked names to replace him.

units.zh: 及安巴堅為主，乃怙強恃勇，不受諸族之代，遂自稱國主。
units.en: Once Abaoji took power, he trusted in his own strength and refused the customary rotation. He proclaimed himself lord of a state in his own right.
units.literal: When Abaoji became lord, he then relied on strength and trusted in valor, would not accept replacement by the tribes, and thus styled himself lord of the state.

units.zh: 天祐四年，大寇雲中，後唐武皇遣使連和，因與之面會於雲中東城，大具享禮，延入帳中，約為兄弟，謂之曰：「唐室為賊所篡，吾欲今冬大舉，弟可以精騎二萬，同收汴、洛。」
units.en: In Tianyou 4 Abaoji invaded Yunzhong in force. The Martial Emperor of Later Tang sent envoys to treat with him and met him at the eastern quarter of Yunzhong city. He laid on a grand feast, brought Abaoji into his tent, and swore brotherhood. "The Tang throne has been seized by traitors," he said. "I mean to strike in force this winter. Brother, bring twenty thousand elite horsemen and we will retake Bian and Luoyang together."
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tianyou he raided Yunzhong on a great scale; the Martial Emperor of Later Tang sent envoys to ally with him, and therefore met him face to face at the eastern city of Yunzhong, lavishly prepared feasting, invited him into the tent, and pledged brotherhood, saying to him: "The house of Tang has been usurped by rebels; I wish this winter to launch a great campaign — younger brother, you may bring twenty thousand picked cavalry and together recover Bian and Luo."

units.zh: 安巴堅許之，賜與甚厚，留馬三千匹以答貺。
units.en: Abaoji agreed. The Martial Emperor lavished gifts upon him, and Abaoji left three thousand horses in return.
units.literal: Abaoji agreed; gifts were very generous, and he left three thousand horses in return for the bounty.

units.zh: 左右咸勸武皇可乘間擄之，武皇曰：「逆賊未殄，不可失信於部落，自亡之道也。」
units.en: His attendants all urged him to seize Abaoji while he could. The Martial Emperor replied, "The rebels are not yet destroyed. I cannot break faith with our tribal allies — that would be the path to ruin."
units.literal: Those at his side all urged the Martial Emperor to seize the chance and capture him; the Martial Emperor said: "The rebellious bandits are not yet destroyed; one must not break faith with the tribes — that is the road to self-destruction."

units.zh: 乃盡禮遣之。
units.en: He therefore sent Abaoji away with full honors.
units.literal: He then with full ceremony sent him away.

units.zh: 及梁祖建號，安巴堅亦遣使送名馬、女樂、貂皮等求封冊。
units.en: When the Liang founder took the throne, Abaoji too sent envoys with fine horses, female musicians, and sable furs, seeking formal recognition from the new dynasty.
units.literal: When the Founder of Liang established his reign title, Abaoji also sent envoys presenting famous horses, female musicians, sable pelts, and the like to seek investiture.

units.zh: 梁祖與之書曰：「朕今天下皆平，唯有太原未服，卿能長驅精甲，徑至新莊，為我翦彼寇讎，與爾便行封冊。」
units.en: The Liang founder wrote to him: "I have pacified the realm except for Taiyuan. If you will ride at speed with your best troops straight to Xinzhuang and destroy that foe for me, I will invest you immediately."
units.literal: The Founder of Liang wrote to him: "I today have pacified all under Heaven; only Taiyuan is not yet subdued. If you can drive picked armor in a long march straight to Xinzhuang and cut down that enemy for me, I will at once carry out investiture for you."

units.zh: 莊宗初嗣世，亦遣使告哀，賂以金繒，求騎軍以救潞州，答其使曰：「我與先王為兄弟，兒即吾兒也，寧有父不助子耶！」
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong first succeeded to the throne, he too sent envoys to announce his father's death, offered gold and silks, and asked for cavalry to relieve Luzhou. Abaoji told the envoy, "Your late sovereign and I were brothers. His son is my son. Would a father refuse to help his own child?"
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong first succeeded to the throne, he also sent envoys to announce mourning, bribed him with gold and silks, and asked for cavalry to rescue Luzhou; he answered the envoy: "I and your late king were brothers — the son is my son; how could a father fail to help his son!"

units.zh: 許出師，會潞平而止。
units.en: He promised to send troops, but Luzhou fell before his army moved and the expedition was called off.
units.literal: He promised to march out; it happened that Luzhou was pacified and he stopped.

units.zh: 劉守光末年苛慘，軍士亡叛皆入契丹。
units.en: In his last years Liu Shouguang ruled with cruelty, and deserters from his ranks flocked to the Khitan.
units.literal: In Liu Shouguang's late years he was harsh and cruel; soldiers who fled and rebelled all entered the Khitan.

units.zh: 洎周德威攻圍幽州。
units.en: When Zhou Dewei laid siege to Youzhou,
units.literal: When Zhou Dewei attacked and besieged Youzhou.

units.zh: 燕之軍民多為所寇掠，既盡得燕中人士，教之文法，由是漸盛。
units.en: the Khitan raided Yan's soldiers and civilians on a wide scale. Having captured the educated men of the Yan region, they taught them administration and law, and from that time their power steadily grew.
units.literal: many soldiers and civilians of Yan were raided and plundered by them; once they had obtained all the men of talent in Yan and taught them written law, from this they gradually grew strong.

units.zh: 十三年八月，阿保機率諸部號稱百萬，自麟、勝陷振武，長驅雲、朔，北邊大擾。
units.en: In the eighth month of year thirteen Abaoji led the tribes in a host said to number a million. He struck from Lin and Sheng, took Zhenwu, and swept through Yun and Shuo, throwing the entire northern frontier into turmoil.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year, Abaoji led the tribes claiming a million men, from Lin and Sheng took Zhenwu, drove straight through Yun and Shuo, and the northern frontier was greatly disturbed.

units.zh: 莊宗赴援於代，敵眾方退。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong marched to relieve them from Dai, and only then did the enemy withdraw.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong went to aid from Dai; the enemy host only then withdrew.

units.zh: 十四年，新州大將盧文進為眾所迫，殺新州團練使李存矩於祁溝關，返攻新、武。
units.en: In year fourteen the Xinzhou general Lu Wenjin, driven by his men, killed the regimental commissioner Li Cunju at Qigou Pass and turned back to attack Xin and Wu prefectures.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year, the great general of Xinzhou Lu Wenjin, pressed by the troops, killed the regimental commissioner of Xinzhou Li Cunju at Qigou Pass, turned back to attack Xin and Wu.

units.zh: 周德威以眾擊之，文進不利，乃奔於契丹，引其眾陷新州。
units.en: Zhou Dewei marched against him, but Wenjin was beaten and fled to the Khitan, leading his forces to seize Xinzhou.
units.literal: Zhou Dewei struck him with troops; Wenjin fared ill and then fled to the Khitan, leading his host to take Xinzhou.

units.zh: 周德威率兵三萬以討之，北騎援新州，德威為敵所敗，殺傷殆盡，契丹乘勝攻幽州。
units.en: Zhou Dewei led thirty thousand men to punish him, but Khitan horsemen relieved Xinzhou. Dewei was routed and his army nearly annihilated. The Khitan pressed their advantage and attacked Youzhou.
units.literal: Zhou Dewei led thirty thousand troops to punish him; northern horsemen relieved Xinzhou, Dewei was defeated by the enemy, killed and wounded nearly all, and the Khitan pressed the victory to attack Youzhou.

units.zh: 是時，或言契丹三十萬，或言五十萬，幽薊之北，所在北騎皆滿。
units.en: Reports at the time put the Khitan at three hundred thousand or even five hundred thousand. North of You and Ji, northern horsemen seemed to fill every road.
units.literal: At that time some said the Khitan were three hundred thousand, some said five hundred thousand; north of You and Ji, wherever one went northern horsemen filled the land.

units.zh: 莊宗遣明宗與李存審、閻寶將兵救幽州，遂解其圍，語在《莊宗紀》中。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong sent Emperor Mingzong, Li Cunshen, and Yan Bao to relieve Youzhou and break the siege. The full account appears in the Basic Annals of Emperor Zhuangzong.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong sent Emperor Mingzong with Li Cunshen and Yan Bao to lead troops to rescue Youzhou, and thus lifted the siege — the account is in the "Basic Annals of Emperor Zhuangzong."

units.zh: 十八年十月，鎮州大將張文禮弒其帥王镕，莊宗討之，時定州王處直與文禮合謀，遣威塞軍使王郁復引契丹為援。
units.en: In the tenth month of year eighteen the Zhenzhou general Zhang Wenli murdered his lord Wang Rong, and Emperor Zhuangzong marched to punish him. Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou joined the plot and sent the Weisai commissioner Wang Yu to bring the Khitan in as allies again.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the eighteenth year, the great general of Zhenzhou Zhang Wenli murdered his commander Wang Rong; Emperor Zhuangzong campaigned against him. At that time Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou conspired with Wenli and sent the Weisai Army commissioner Wang Yu to again lead the Khitan as reinforcements.

units.zh: 十二月，安巴堅傾塞入寇，攻圍幽州，李紹宏以兵城守。
units.en: In the twelfth month Abaoji invaded in force, besieged Youzhou, and Li Shaohong held the city with the garrison.
units.literal: In the twelfth month, Abaoji poured across the frontier in invasion, attacked and besieged Youzhou, and Li Shaohong defended the city with troops.

units.zh: 契丹長驅陷涿郡，執刺史李嗣弼，進攻易、定，至新樂，渡沙河，王都遣使告急。
units.en: The Khitan swept south, took Zhuo, captured Prefect Li Sibi, and pressed Yi and Ding. They reached Xinle, crossed the Sha River, and Wang Du sent desperate appeals for help.
units.literal: The Khitan drove straight through and took Zhuo commandery, seized Prefect Li Sibi, advanced to attack Yi and Ding, reached Xinle, crossed the Sha River, and Wang Du sent envoys in urgent appeal.

units.zh: 時莊宗在鎮州行營，聞前鋒報日「敵渡沙河」，軍中鹹恐，議者請權釋鎮州之圍以避之。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong was then at his field camp before Zhenzhou. When the vanguard reported, "The enemy has crossed the Sha River," panic spread through the army, and some urged him to raise the siege of Zhenzhou and withdraw.
units.literal: At that time Emperor Zhuangzong was at the field headquarters in Zhenzhou; hearing the vanguard report say "the enemy has crossed the Sha River," the army all feared, and advisers asked temporarily to lift the siege of Zhenzhou to avoid them.

units.zh: 莊宗曰：「霸王舉事，自有天道，契丹其如我何！
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong said, "When a true conqueror takes the field, Heaven itself is on his side. What can the Khitan do to me?
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong said: "When a hegemon-king undertakes affairs, Heaven has its own way — what can the Khitan do to me!

units.zh: 國初，突厥入寇，至於渭北，高祖欲棄長安，遷都樊、鄧，太守曰：「獫狁孔熾，自古有之，未聞遷移都邑。
units.en: At the founding of Tang, when the Turks raided as far as the north bank of the Wei, Gaozu wanted to abandon Chang'an for Fan and Deng. Taizong said, "The northern tribes have always been fierce. That is no reason to move the capital.
units.literal: At the founding of the state, the Turks invaded and reached north of the Wei; Gaozu wished to abandon Chang'an and move the capital to Fan and Deng. Taizong said: "The Xianyun have always burned fiercely — from antiquity it has been so; one has never heard of moving the capital.

units.zh: 霍去病，漢廷將帥，猶且誌滅匈奴，況帝王應運，而欲移都避寇哉！」
units.en: Huo Qubing was only a Han general, yet he burned to destroy the Xiongnu. How could an emperor who holds Heaven's mandate think of fleeing the capital before mere raiders?"
units.literal: Huo Qubing, a general of the Han court, still aspired to destroy the Xiongnu — how much more a sovereign who receives Heaven's mandate, yet would move the capital to flee bandits!"

units.zh: 文皇雄武，不數年俘二突厥為衛士。
units.en: Emperor Taizong was bold in war. Within a few years he had captured both Turk khans and made them his palace guards.
units.literal: Emperor Taizong was heroic and martial; within a few years he captured both Turks and made them palace guards.

units.zh: 今吾以數萬之眾安集山東，王德明廝養小人，阿保機生長邊地，豈有退避之理，吾何面視蒼生哉！
units.en: I hold Shandong secure with tens of thousands of men. Wang Deming is a groom's lackey, and Abaoji is a frontier barbarian. Why should I retreat? How could I face the people of this land?
units.literal: Now I with tens of thousands of men have settled Shandong in peace — Wang Deming is a menial groom's petty man, Abaoji grew up on the frontier; is there any reason to retreat? How could I face the black-haired people!

units.zh: 爾曹但駕馬同行，看吾破敵。」
units.en: Mount up and ride with me. Watch me break the enemy."
units.literal: You lot need only mount your horses and come along — watch me break the enemy."

units.zh: 莊宗親禦鐵騎五千，至新城北，遇契丹前鋒萬騎，莊宗精甲自桑林突出，光明照日，諸部愕然緩退，莊宗分二廣以乘之，敵騎散退。
units.en: He personally led five thousand armored horsemen to the north of Xincheng and met ten thousand Khitan vanguard troops. His elite cavalry burst from Mulberry Grove, armor flashing in the sun. The Khitan clans faltered and fell back. Zhuangzong split his force in two wings, routed them, and the enemy scattered.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong personally led five thousand iron cavalry to north of Xincheng, met ten thousand Khitan vanguard horsemen; Zhuangzong's picked armor burst from Mulberry Grove, light shining on the sun, the tribes stunned and slowing their retreat; Zhuangzong divided two wings to strike them, and the enemy horsemen scattered and withdrew.

units.zh: 時沙河微冰，其馬多陷，安巴堅退保望都。
units.en: The Sha River had only thin ice, and many Khitan horses foundered. Abaoji fell back to Wangdu.
units.literal: At that time the Sha River had thin ice; many of their horses sank in; Abaoji withdrew to defend Wangdu.

units.zh: 是夜，莊宗次定州，翌日出戰，遇奚長托諾五千騎，莊宗親軍千騎與之鬥，為其所圍，外救不及，莊宗挺馬奮躍，出入數四，酣戰不解。
units.en: That night he camped at Dingzhou. The next day he gave battle and met the Xi chief Tuonuo with five thousand horsemen. A thousand of Zhuangzong's personal guard engaged them, were surrounded, and no relief could reach them in time. Zhuangzong spurred his horse and charged in and out of the ring four times, fighting on without pause.
units.literal: That night Emperor Zhuangzong halted at Dingzhou; the next day he went out to battle, met the Xi chief Tuonuo with five thousand horsemen; Zhuangzong's personal guard of one thousand horsemen fought them, was surrounded by them, outside rescue could not reach in time; Zhuangzong spurred his horse and leaped fiercely, going in and out four times, fighting fiercely without resolution.

units.zh: 李嗣昭聞其急也，灑泣而往，攻破敵陣，掖莊宗而歸。
units.en: Li Sizhao, hearing that he was in peril, rode forward in tears, broke the enemy line, and brought Emperor Zhuangzong back to safety.
units.literal: Li Sizhao, hearing he was in peril, went with tears streaming, broke the enemy formation, and supported Emperor Zhuangzong back.

units.zh: 時契丹值大雪，野無所掠，馬無芻草，凍死者相望於路。
units.en: Heavy snow fell on the Khitan. Nothing remained to plunder in the fields, fodder ran out, and frozen corpses lined the road as far as the eye could see.
units.literal: At that time the Khitan encountered great snow; in the wilds there was nothing to plunder, horses had no fodder grass, and those frozen to death lined the road in sight of one another.

units.zh: 安巴堅召盧文進，以手指天謂之曰：「天未令我到此。」
units.en: Abaoji summoned Lu Wenjin, pointed to the sky, and said, "Heaven did not will me to come this far."
units.literal: Abaoji summoned Lu Wenjin, pointed to Heaven with his finger and said to him: "Heaven has not yet willed me to come here."

units.zh: 乃引眾北去。
units.en: He then led his army north.
units.literal: He then led the host north away.

units.zh: 莊宗率精兵騎躡其後，每經安巴堅野宿之所，布稭在地，方而環之，雖去，無一莖亂者，莊宗謂左右曰：「蕃人法令如是，豈中國所及！」
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong pursued with elite cavalry. At every camp Abaoji had used, the straw was laid in neat squares and rings; even after the Khitan had gone, not a stalk was out of place. Zhuangzong told his attendants, "Their discipline is like this. China cannot match it."
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong led picked cavalry in pursuit behind them; wherever he passed Abaoji's camps in the wild, straw was spread on the ground in squares and circled — though they had gone, not a single stalk was disordered. Emperor Zhuangzong said to those at his side: "Barbarian law and order are like this — how could China match it!"

units.zh: 莊宗至幽州，發二百騎偵之，皆為契丹所獲，莊宗乃還。
units.en: He reached Youzhou and sent two hundred horsemen to scout. The Khitan captured them all, and he turned back.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong reached Youzhou, sent out two hundred horsemen to scout — all were captured by the Khitan — and Zhuangzong then returned.

units.zh: 天祐末，安巴堅乃自稱皇帝，署中國官號。
units.en: Late in the Tianyou era Abaoji proclaimed himself emperor and created offices on the Chinese model.
units.literal: At the end of Tianyou, Abaoji then styled himself emperor and appointed Chinese official titles.

units.zh: 其俗舊隨畜牧，素無邑屋，得燕人所教，乃為城郭宮室之制於漠北，距幽州三千里，名其邑曰西樓邑，屋門皆東向，如車帳之法。
units.en: They had always lived as nomads and built no permanent towns until men from Yan taught them. Abaoji then raised walled cities and palaces in the northern steppe three thousand li from Youzhou. He called his capital Western Tower. Every doorway faced east, as with their wagon tents.
units.literal: Their custom had long followed pastoral herding and they had never had towns or houses; taught by men of Yan, they then made the system of walled cities and palaces in the northern desert, three thousand li from Youzhou, naming their settlement Western Tower Settlement; house doors all faced east, like the method of cart tents.

units.zh: 城南別作一城，以實漢人，名曰漢城，城中有佛寺三，僧尼千人。
units.en: South of the capital he built a separate city for Han subjects called Han City. It held three Buddhist temples and a thousand monks and nuns.
units.literal: South of the city they separately built another city to house Han people, called Han City; within the city were three Buddhist temples and a thousand monks and nuns.

units.zh: 其國人號安巴堅為天皇王。
units.en: His people called Abaoji the Heavenly Emperor King.
units.literal: The people of his state called Abaoji the Heavenly Emperor King.

units.zh: 同光中，安巴堅深著辟地之志，欲收兵大舉，慮渤海踵其後。
units.en: During Tongguang, Abaoji was bent on expansion and meant to gather his armies for a major campaign, but he feared that Bohai would strike at his rear.
units.literal: In the Tongguang era, Abaoji deeply harbored ambition to open territory, wished to gather troops for a great campaign, and feared Bohai would follow at his heels.

units.zh: 三年，舉其眾討渤海之遼東，令禿餒、盧文進據營、平等州，擾我燕薊。
units.en: In year three he marched in force against Bohai's Liaodong. He left Tunei and Lu Wenjin to hold Ying, Ping, and neighboring prefectures and raid Yan and Ji.
units.literal: In the third year he raised his host to campaign against Bohai's Liaodong, ordered Tunei and Lu Wenjin to hold Ying and Ping and other prefectures, and harass our Yan and Ji.

units.zh: 明宗初纂嗣，遣供奉官姚坤奉書告哀，至西樓邑，屬阿保機在渤海，又徑至慎州，崎嶇萬里。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong first took the throne, he sent the palace attendant Yao Kun with a letter of condolence. Kun reached Western Tower, learned that Abaoji was campaigning in Bohai, and pressed on to Shenzhou across ten thousand li of hard country.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong first succeeded to the throne, he sent the palace attendant Yao Kun to present a letter announcing mourning; he reached Western Tower Settlement — it happened that Abaoji was in Bohai — and again went straight to Shenzhou, ten thousand li of rugged travel.

units.zh: 既至，謁見阿保機，延入穹廬，阿保機身長九尺，被錦袍，大帶垂後，與妻對榻引見坤。
units.en: When he arrived he was received by Abaoji in the royal tent. Abaoji stood nine chi tall, wore a brocade robe with a great belt hanging behind him, and with his wife on a facing couch received Kun.
units.literal: When he arrived he had audience with Abaoji, who invited him into the domed tent; Abaoji was nine chi in height, wore a brocade robe, a great belt hanging behind, and with his wife on facing couches received and introduced Kun.

units.zh: 坤未致命，阿保機先問曰：「聞爾漢土河南、河北各有一天子，信乎？」
units.en: Before Kun could deliver his message, Abaoji asked, "I hear that your Han lands now have one Son of Heaven south of the Yellow River and another north of it. Is that true?"
units.literal: Before Kun could deliver his charge, Abaoji first asked: "I hear that in your Han lands south of the river and north of the river each has a Son of Heaven — is it true?"

units.zh: 坤曰：「河南天子，今年四月一日洛陽軍變，今兇問至矣。
units.en: Kun said, "The Son of Heaven south of the river died in a military mutiny at Luoyang on the first day of the fourth month this year. The grievous news has only now reached us.
units.literal: Kun said: "The Son of Heaven south of the river — this year on the first day of the fourth month there was a military mutiny at Luoyang; now the grievous news has arrived.

units.zh: 河北總管令公，比為魏州軍亂，先帝詔令除討，既聞內難，軍眾離心，及京城無主，上下堅冊令公，請主社稷，今已順人望登帝位矣。」
units.en: The chief commander north of the river, Lord Ling, had lately been ordered by the late emperor to suppress the Weizhou mutiny. When he heard of the turmoil in the capital, his troops lost heart. With the throne empty, his officers and men pressed him to take the throne, and he has now ascended in accord with their will."
units.literal: The Chief Commander north of the river, Lord Ling — recently because of the Weizhou military mutiny the late emperor issued an edict ordering him to suppress it; once he heard of internal troubles, the army and masses lost heart, and when the capital had no lord, high and low firmly enthroned Lord Ling and asked him to preside over the altars of soil and grain — he has now followed the people's hope and ascended the imperial throne."

units.zh: 阿保機號咷，聲淚俱發，曰：「我與河東先世約為兄弟，河南天子吾兒也。
units.en: Abaoji broke into loud wailing, voice and tears together, and said, "Your late sovereign of Hedong and I were sworn brothers. The Son of Heaven south of the river was my son.
units.literal: Abaoji wailed aloud, voice and tears together bursting forth, and said: "I and the late lord of Hedong pledged brotherhood — the Son of Heaven south of the river was my son.

units.zh: 近聞漢地兵亂，點得甲馬五萬騎，比欲自往洛陽救助我兒，又緣渤海未下，我兒果致如此，冤哉！」
units.en: When I heard of the turmoil in your lands I gathered fifty thousand horsemen and was about to ride to Luoyang myself to save my son, but Bohai was not yet conquered. And now my son has come to this. How unjust!"
units.literal: Recently hearing of military turmoil in Han lands, I mustered fifty thousand armored horses and had just intended to go myself to Luoyang to rescue my son, but again because Bohai was not yet subdued, my son truly came to this — how unjust!"

units.zh: 泣下不能已。
units.en: He wept without cease.
units.literal: Tears fell and he could not stop.

units.zh: 又謂坤曰：「今漢土天子，初聞洛陽有難，不急救，致令及此。」
units.en: He told Kun again, "Your new emperor heard of the disaster at Luoyang and did not hurry to help. That is how things came to this pass."
units.literal: He again said to Kun: "Now the Son of Heaven of Han lands, when he first heard of trouble at Luoyang, did not rush to rescue — causing it to reach this."

units.zh: 坤曰：「非不急切，地遠阻隔不及也。」
units.en: Kun said, "It was not for lack of urgency. The distance was too great and we could not arrive in time."
units.literal: Kun said: "It was not that we were not urgent — the distance was far and barriers blocked; we could not arrive in time."

units.zh: 又曰：「我兒既殂，當合取我商量，安得自便！」
units.en: He said again, "Now that my son is dead, you should have consulted me. How could you decide on your own?"
units.literal: He again said: "Since my son has died, you ought to have consulted me — how could you act on your own!"

units.zh: 坤曰：「吾皇將兵二十年，位至大總管，所部精兵三十萬，眾口一心，聖堅推戴，違之則立見禍生，非不知稟天皇王意旨，無奈人心何。」
units.en: Kun said, "Our emperor has led armies for twenty years and commands three hundred thousand elite troops. Every man under him spoke as one. They pressed him to the throne, and to refuse would have brought immediate ruin. We do not ignore the Heavenly Emperor King's wishes, but we could not defy the will of the army."
units.literal: Kun said: "Our emperor has commanded troops for twenty years, risen to Great Chief Commander, has three hundred thousand picked troops under him, every mouth with one heart — the sage was firmly pushed to the throne; to disobey would at once bring disaster — it is not that we did not know to defer to the Heavenly Emperor King's intent, but we were helpless before the people's will."

units.zh: 其子托雲在側，謂坤曰：「漢使勿多談。」
units.en: His son Tuoyun, standing beside him, said to Kun, "Han envoy, say no more."
units.literal: His son Tuoyun was at his side and said to Kun: "Han envoy, do not talk overmuch."

units.zh: 因引左氏牽牛蹊田之說以折坤，坤曰：「應天順人，不同匹夫之義，只如天皇王初領國事，豈是強取之耶！」
units.en: He cited the Zuo Commentary tale of the oxherd who trampled another's fields to rebuke Kun. Kun replied, "To follow Heaven and win the people's assent is not the same as a private quarrel. When you first took power, Heavenly Emperor King, was that by force alone?"
units.literal: He then cited from the Zuo Commentary the story of the oxherd trampling fields to refute Kun; Kun said: "Answering Heaven and following the people is not the same as a common man's righteousness — just as when the Heavenly Emperor King first took charge of state affairs, was it by force that he took it!"

units.zh: 阿保機因曰：「理當如此，我漢國兒子致有此難，我知之矣。
units.en: Abaoji said, "That is only right. I know now why my Han son came to this end.
units.literal: Abaoji then said: "It ought to be so — my Han-state son brought this trouble on himself; I understand it now.

units.zh: 聞此兒有宮婢二千，樂官千人，終日放鷹走狗，耽酒嗜色，不惜人民，任使不肖，致得天下皆怒。
units.en: I hear he kept two thousand palace women and a thousand musicians, spent his days hawking and hunting, drowned himself in wine and women, wasted the people, and put worthless men in office until the whole realm turned against him.
units.literal: I heard this son had two thousand palace maids and a thousand music officers, all day released hawks and coursed dogs, indulged in wine and favored women, did not cherish the people, employed the unworthy at will, and thereby made all under Heaven angry.

units.zh: 我自聞如斯，常憂傾覆，一月前已有人來報，知我兒有事，我便舉家斷酒，解放鷹犬，休罷樂官。
units.en: When I heard such things I feared ruin for my own house. A month ago a messenger told me my son was in danger. I forbade wine in my household, released my hawks and dogs, and dismissed my musicians.
units.literal: When I myself heard it was so, I constantly feared overthrow; a month ago someone had already come to report, knowing my son was in trouble — I then had the whole household cut off wine, released hawks and dogs, and dismissed the music officers.

units.zh: 我亦有諸部家樂千人，非公宴未嘗妄舉。
units.en: I too have a thousand household musicians among the tribes, and I never call for music except at state feasts.
units.literal: I too have a thousand household musicians of the tribes, and except at public feasts I never raise them rashly.

units.zh: 我若所為似我兒，亦應不能持久矣，從此願以為戒。」
units.en: If I acted as my son did, I could not have endured either. From this day I take his fate as my warning."
units.literal: If what I did were like my son, I too could not have lasted long — from now on I wish to take this as a warning.

units.zh: 又曰：「漢國兒與我雖父子，亦曾彼此讎敵，俱有惡心，與爾今天子無惡，足得歡好。
units.en: He said again, "That Han son and I were father and son in name, yet we were enemies at heart. With your present emperor there is no such ill will. We can be good friends.
units.literal: He again said: "The Han-state son and I, though father and son, were also once mutual enemies — both had ill will; with your present Son of Heaven there is no ill will — enough to be on friendly terms.

units.zh: 爾先復命，我續將馬萬騎至幽、鎮以南，與爾家天子面為盟約，我要幽州，令漢兒把捉，更不復侵入漢界。」
units.en: Return first with your report. I will follow with ten thousand horsemen south of You and Zhen to swear alliance with your emperor in person. I want Youzhou held by Han men, and I will not cross the Han frontier again."
units.literal: You first return with your report; I will then lead ten thousand horses south of You and Zhen to make a face-to-face covenant with your house's Son of Heaven — I want Youzhou and will have Han men hold it, and will no longer invade Han territory."

units.zh: 又問：「漢收得西川，信不？」
units.en: He asked again, "Is it true that you have taken western Shu?"
units.literal: He again asked: "The Han have taken western Shu — is it true?"

units.zh: 坤曰：「去年九月出兵，十一月十六日收下東、西川，得兵馬二十萬，金帛無算。
units.en: Kun said, "Our armies marched last year in the ninth month and on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month took both eastern and western Shu. We gained two hundred thousand troops and horses and untold gold and silks.
units.literal: Kun said: "Last year in the ninth month troops were sent out; on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month eastern and western Shu were taken, obtaining two hundred thousand troops and horses, gold and silks beyond counting.

units.zh: 皇帝初即位，未辦送來，續當遣使至矣。」
units.en: The emperor has only just taken the throne and has not yet been able to send tribute, but envoys will follow soon."
units.literal: The emperor has just ascended the throne and has not yet been able to send them; envoys will be dispatched presently."

units.zh: 阿保機忻然曰：「聞西有劍閣，兵馬從何過得？」
units.en: Abaoji said with delight, "I have heard of Sword Pass in the west. How could an army pass it?"
units.literal: Abaoji said with pleasure: "I hear in the west there is Sword Pass — how could troops and horses get through?"

units.zh: 坤曰：「川路雖險，然先朝收復河南，有精兵四十萬，良馬十萬騎，但通人行處，便能去得，視劍閣如平地耳。」
units.en: Kun said, "The Shu roads are steep, but when the former dynasty recovered Henan it had four hundred thousand elite troops and one hundred thousand fine horses. Wherever a man can walk, an army can go. Sword Pass is level ground to us."
units.literal: Kun said: "Though the Shu roads are perilous, yet when the former dynasty recovered Henan it had four hundred thousand picked troops and one hundred thousand fine horses — wherever a man can pass, one can go; Sword Pass is regarded as level ground."

units.zh: 阿保機善漢語，謂坤曰：「吾解漢語，歷口不敢言，懼部人效我，令兵士怯弱故也。」
units.en: Abaoji was fluent in Chinese. He told Kun, "I understand your language, but I have never dared speak it openly, lest my tribes imitate me and my warriors grow soft."
units.literal: Abaoji was skilled in Han speech and said to Kun: "I understand Han speech, but through all my days I dared not speak it, fearing the tribes would imitate me and make the soldiers timid and weak."

units.zh: 坤至止三日，阿保機病傷寒。
units.en: Kun had been there only three days when Abaoji fell ill with a fever.
units.literal: Kun had been there only three days when Abaoji fell ill with cold damage.

units.zh: 一夕，大星殞於其帳前，俄而卒於扶餘城，時天成元年七月二十七日也。
units.en: One night a great star fell before his tent. Soon afterward he died at Fuyu city, on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month of Tiancheng 1.
units.literal: One night a great star fell before his tent; shortly he died at Fuyu city — the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month of Tiancheng 1.

units.zh: 其妻舒嚕氏自率眾護其喪歸西樓，坤亦從行，得報而還。
units.en: His wife Lady Shulü led the funeral train back to Western Tower. Kun accompanied them, received word of the death, and returned.
units.literal: His wife Lady Shulü herself led the host to escort the bier back to Western Tower; Kun also followed on the journey, received the report, and returned.

units.zh: 既而舒嚕氏立其次子德光為渠帥，以總國事，尋遣使告哀，明宗為之輟朝。
units.en: Lady Shulü then installed her second son Deguang as chief to govern the state. She soon sent envoys to announce the death, and Emperor Mingzong suspended court in mourning.
units.literal: Shortly Lady Shulü enthroned her second son Deguang as tribal chief to oversee state affairs; soon she sent envoys to announce mourning, and Emperor Mingzong suspended court for it.

units.zh: 明年正月，葬阿保機於木葉山，偽謚曰「大聖皇帝」。
units.en: In the first month of the following year they buried Abaoji on Mount Muye and gave him the posthumous title "Great Sage Emperor."
units.literal: In the first month of the following year they buried Abaoji on Mount Muye; his false posthumous title was "Great Sage Emperor."

units.zh: 阿保機凡三子，皆雄偉。
units.en: Abaoji had three sons, all imposing men.
units.literal: Abaoji had three sons in all, all imposing in stature.

units.zh: 長曰人皇王突然，即東丹王也；
units.en: The eldest was called Human Emperor King Turan, the King of Eastern Dan;
units.literal: The eldest was called Human Emperor King Turan — that is, the King of Eastern Dan;

units.zh: 次曰元帥太子，即德光也；
units.en: the second was Marshal Crown Prince Deguang;
units.literal: the second was called Marshal Crown Prince — that is, Deguang;

units.zh: 幼曰阿安端君。
units.en: the youngest was Lord Aanduan.
units.literal: the youngest was called Lord Aanduan.

units.zh: 德光本名耀屈之，後慕中華文字，遂改焉。
units.en: Deguang had originally been named Yaokuizhi, but later he admired Chinese writing and took a new name.
units.literal: Deguang's original name was Yaokuizhi; later he admired Chinese script and therefore changed it.

units.zh: 唐天成初，阿保機死，其母令德光權主牙帳，令少子安端少君往渤海國代突欲。
units.en: Early in Tiancheng, when Abaoji died, his mother had Deguang govern the tribal camp in his stead and sent the youngest son, Young Lord Anduan, to Bohai to replace Tuyu.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tang's Tiancheng, when Abaoji died, his mother had Deguang provisionally preside over the tribal encampment and sent the younger son Young Lord Anduan to the Bohai state to replace Tuyu.

units.zh: 突欲將立，而德光素為部族所服，又其母亦常鐘愛，故因而立之。
units.en: Tuyu had been expected to succeed, but the tribes had long respected Deguang, and his mother favored him, so Deguang was enthroned instead.
units.literal: Tuyu was about to be installed, but Deguang had long been obeyed by the tribes, and his mother also constantly favored him, and therefore he was installed instead.

units.zh: 明宗時，德光遣使摩琳等三十餘人來修好，又遣使為父求碑石，明宗許之，賜與甚厚，並賜其母瓔珞錦彩。
units.en: During Mingzong's reign Deguang sent more than thirty envoys led by Molin to renew relations and asked for a memorial stele for his father. Mingzong agreed, lavished gifts upon them, and sent brocades and jeweled necklaces to Deguang's mother.
units.literal: In Emperor Mingzong's time, Deguang sent envoys Molin and more than thirty others to renew friendly relations, and again sent envoys to seek a stone stele for his father; Emperor Mingzong granted it, gifts were very generous, and he also bestowed on his mother necklaces and brocades.

units.zh: 自是山北安靜，蕃漢不相侵擾。
units.en: From that time the country north of the mountains was at peace, and Khitan and Han did not raid one another.
units.literal: From then on the lands north of the mountains were quiet, and barbarians and Han did not harass each other.

units.zh: 三年，德光偽改為天顯元年。
units.en: In year three Deguang proclaimed the Tianxian era.
units.literal: In the third year Deguang falsely changed the era to Tianxian 1.

units.zh: 是歲，定州王都作亂，求援於契丹，德光陷平州，遣禿餒以騎五千援都於中山，招討使王晏球破之於曲陽，托諾走保賊城。
units.en: That year Wang Du of Dingzhou rebelled and called on the Khitan for help. Deguang took Pingzhou and sent Tunei with five thousand horsemen to relieve Du at Zhongshan. The pacification commissioner Wang Yanqiu defeated them at Quyang, and Tuonuo fled into the rebel city.
units.literal: That year Wang Du of Dingzhou rebelled and sought aid from the Khitan; Deguang took Pingzhou, sent Tunei with five thousand horsemen to aid Du at Zhongshan; the pacification commissioner Wang Yanqiu defeated them at Quyang, and Tuonuo fled to hold the rebel city.

units.zh: 其年七月，又遣惕隱率七千騎救定州，王晏球逆戰於唐河北，大破之。
units.en: In the seventh month he sent the Tiyiin with seven thousand horsemen to relieve Dingzhou again. Wang Yanqiu met them on the north bank of the Tang River and crushed them.
units.literal: In the seventh month of that year he again sent the Tiyiin leading seven thousand horsemen to rescue Dingzhou; Wang Yanqiu met them in battle on the north bank of the Tang River and routed them greatly.

units.zh: 幽州趙德鈞以生兵接於要路，生擒惕隱等首領五十餘人獻闕下。
units.en: Zhao Dejun of Youzhou blocked the vital road with fresh troops, captured more than fifty Khitan leaders including the Tiyiin, and sent them to the imperial court.
units.literal: Zhao Dejun of Youzhou with fresh troops blocked the vital road, captured alive more than fifty leaders including the Tiyiin, and presented them at court.

units.zh: 明年，王都平，擒托諾及餘眾，斬之。
units.en: The following year Wang Du's rebellion was crushed. Tuonuo and his remaining followers were captured and executed.
units.literal: The next year Wang Du was pacified; Tuonuo and the remaining host were captured and beheaded.

units.zh: 自是契丹大挫，數年不敢窺邊。
units.en: From that defeat the Khitan did not dare probe the border again for years.
units.literal: From then on the Khitan suffered a great setback and for several years did not dare peer at the frontier.

units.zh: 嘗遣使挎括梅裏來求禿餒骸骨，明宗怒其詐，斬之。
units.en: They once sent an envoy named Kuakuomeili to demand Tunei's remains. Mingzong, furious at the imposture, had him executed.
units.literal: They once sent the envoy Kuakuomeili to seek Tunei's bones; Emperor Mingzong, angered at the deceit, beheaded him.

units.zh: 長興二年，東丹王突欲在闕下，其母繼發使申報，朝廷亦優容之。
units.en: In Changxing 2 the King of Eastern Dan, Tuyu, was at the Tang court. His mother kept sending envoys with reports, and the court treated him leniently.
units.literal: In the second year of Changxing, Eastern Dan King Tuyu was at court; his mother continued to send envoys to report, and the court also treated him with indulgence.

units.zh: 長興末，契丹迫雲州，明宗命晉高祖為河東節度使兼北面蕃漢總管。
units.en: Late in Changxing the Khitan pressed Yunzhou. Mingzong appointed the future Jin founder military governor of Hedong and commander of all northern barbarian and Han forces.
units.literal: Late in Changxing the Khitan pressed Yunzhou; Emperor Mingzong appointed the Jin Founder as military governor of Hedong and concurrently chief of northern barbarian and Han affairs.

units.zh: 清泰三年，晉高祖為張敬達等攻圍甚急，遣指揮使何福賫表乞師，願為臣子。
units.en: In Qingtai 3 the Jin founder was besieged by Zhang Jingda and others. He sent Commander He Fu with a petition begging for Khitan aid and offering to become their vassal.
units.literal: In the third year of Qingtai the Jin Founder was pressed hard in siege by Zhang Jingda and others; he sent the commander He Fu with a memorial begging troops and offering to become a subject.

units.zh: 德光白其母曰：「兒昨夢太原石郎發使到國，今果至矣，事符天意，必須赴之。」
units.en: Deguang told his mother, "I dreamed last night that Lord Stone of Taiyuan was sending envoys to us. They have come. Heaven wills this. I must go."
units.literal: Deguang told his mother: "Yesterday I dreamed that Stone Lord of Taiyuan sent envoys to our state — now they have truly arrived; the matter matches Heaven's intent — I must go to them."

units.zh: 德光乃自率五萬騎由雁門至晉陽，即日大破敬達之眾於城下，尋冊晉高祖為大晉皇帝，約為父子之國，割幽州管內及新、武、雲、應、朔州之地以賂之，仍每歲許輸帛三十萬。
units.en: Deguang led fifty thousand horsemen through Yanmen to Jinyang and the same day routed Zhang Jingda beneath the walls. He then enthroned the Jin founder as emperor of Great Jin, pledged a father-and-son alliance, ceded the Sixteen Prefectures including Youzhou, Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, and Shuo, and promised three hundred thousand bolts of silk each year.
units.literal: Deguang then personally led fifty thousand horsemen through Yanmen to Jinyang, the same day routing Jingda's host below the city; soon he enthroned the Jin Founder as Great Jin Emperor, pledged a father-and-son state, ceded lands within Youzhou circuit and Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, and Shuo prefectures as bribes, and moreover each year promised to deliver three hundred thousand bolts of silk.

units.zh: 時幽州趙德鈞屯兵於團柏谷，遣使至幕帳，求立己為帝，以石氏世襲太原，德光對使指帳前一石曰：「我已許石郎為父子之盟，石爛可改矣。」
units.en: Zhao Dejun of Youzhou was encamped at Tuanbai Valley and sent envoys offering to make him emperor if the Shi family kept Taiyuan in perpetuity. Deguang pointed at a stone before his tent and said, "I have sworn a father-and-son bond with Lord Stone. Only when stone rots may that bond change."
units.literal: At that time Zhao Dejun of Youzhou encamped at Tuanbai Valley, sent envoys to the tent headquarters, asked to be enthroned himself with the Shi clan hereditarily holding Taiyuan; Deguang answered the envoy, pointing at a stone before the tent: "I have already pledged a father-and-son alliance with Lord Stone — when stone rots it may change."

units.zh: 楊光遠等殺張敬達降於契丹，德光戲謂光遠等曰：「爾輩大是惡漢兒，不用鹽酪，食卻一萬匹戰馬。」
units.en: Yang Guangyuan and others killed Zhang Jingda and surrendered. Deguang joked to them, "You wicked Han — you won't touch salt or dairy, yet you've devoured ten thousand of our war horses."
units.literal: Yang Guangyuan and others killed Zhang Jingda and surrendered to the Khitan; Deguang jested to Guangyuan and the rest: "You lot are truly wicked Han fellows — you use no salt or curds, yet you have eaten up ten thousand war horses."

units.zh: 光遠等大慚。
units.en: They were deeply ashamed.
units.literal: Guangyuan and the rest were deeply ashamed.

units.zh: 晉高祖南行，德光自送至潞州。
units.en: The Jin founder marched south, and Deguang escorted him as far as Luzhou.
units.literal: The Jin Founder went south; Deguang personally escorted him to Luzhou.

units.zh: 時趙德鈞、趙延壽自潞州出降於契丹，德光鎖之，令隨牙帳。
units.en: Zhao Dejun and Zhao Yanshou surrendered at Luzhou. Deguang put them in chains and kept them with his camp.
units.literal: At that time Zhao Dejun and Zhao Yanshou came out from Luzhou and surrendered to the Khitan; Deguang put them in fetters and ordered them to follow the tribal encampment.

units.zh: 晉高祖入洛，尋遣宰相趙瑩致謝於契丹。
units.en: The Jin founder entered Luoyang and soon sent Chancellor Zhao Ying to thank the Khitan court.
units.literal: The Jin Founder entered Luoyang and soon sent Chancellor Zhao Ying to express thanks to the Khitan.

units.zh: 天福三年，又遣宰臣馮道、左僕射劉句等持節冊德光及其母氏徽號，賫鹵簿、儀伏、法服、車輅於本國行禮。
units.en: In Tianfu 3 he sent Chancellor Feng Dao and Left Vice Director Liu Gou with credentials to invest Deguang and his mother with honorific titles, bearing full imperial regalia to conduct the ceremony in the Khitan homeland.
units.literal: In Tianfu 3 he again sent Chancellor Feng Dao, Left Vice Director Liu Gou, and others bearing credentials to invest Deguang and his mother with honorific titles, carrying regalia, ritual guards, court robes, and chariots to perform the ceremony in their own state.

units.zh: 德光大悅，尋遣使奉晉高祖為英武明義皇帝。
units.en: Deguang was delighted and in return honored the Jin founder as Heroic Martial Enlightened Righteous Emperor.
units.literal: Deguang was greatly pleased and soon sent envoys to honor the Jin Founder as Heroic Martial Enlightened Righteous Emperor.

units.zh: 是歲，契丹改天顯十一年為會同元年，以趙延壽為樞密使，升幽州為南京，以趙思溫為南京留守，既而德光請晉高祖不稱臣，不上表，來往緘題止用家人禮，但云「兒皇帝」，晉祖厚賫金帛以謝之。
units.en: That year the Khitan proclaimed the Huitong era, made Zhao Yanshou Grand Councilor, elevated Youzhou to Southern Capital with Zhao Siwen as regent, and persuaded the Jin court to drop the language of vassalage. Their letters used family terms only, calling the Jin ruler "Son Emperor." The Jin founder paid lavish gifts in gratitude.
units.literal: That year the Khitan changed Tianxian 11 to Huitong 1, appointed Zhao Yanshou Grand Councilor, elevated Youzhou to Southern Capital, appointed Zhao Siwen Southern Capital regent; shortly Deguang asked the Jin Founder not to call himself subject or submit memorials — correspondence used only family rites, merely saying "Son Emperor" — the Jin ancestor richly rewarded gold and silks in thanks.

units.zh: 晉祖奉契丹甚至，歲時問遺，慶吊之禮，必令優厚。
units.en: The Jin founder courted the Khitan with extreme deference. Seasonal gifts and rites of congratulation and mourning were always sent in lavish measure.
units.literal: The Jin ancestor served the Khitan to the utmost; seasonal greetings and gifts, rites of congratulation and condolence — all were ordered generous.

units.zh: 每北使至，即於別殿致敬。
units.en: Whenever Khitan envoys arrived, he received them with ceremony in a separate hall.
units.literal: Whenever northern envoys arrived, he at once paid respects in a separate hall.

units.zh: 德光每有邀請，小不如意，則來譴責，晉祖每屈己以奉之，終晉祖世，略無釁隙。
units.en: If the slightest request went unmet, Deguang sent rebukes. The Jin founder always humbled himself to comply. Through his reign there was almost no open rupture.
units.literal: Whenever Deguang had invitations, if slightly displeased he would come to rebuke; the Jin ancestor each time humbled himself to serve him — through the Jin ancestor's lifetime there was scarcely any breach.

units.zh: 及少帝嗣位，遣使入契丹，德光以少帝不先承稟，擅即尊位，所賫文字，略去臣禮，大怒，形於責讓，朝廷使去，即加譴辱。
units.en: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he sent envoys to the Khitan. Deguang was furious that the new ruler had taken the throne without his leave and that the letters omitted the language of vassalage. He rebuked them openly and insulted every envoy who departed.
units.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne he sent envoys to the Khitan; Deguang, because the Young Emperor had not first reported for approval but seized the throne on his own, and the documents presented omitted subject rites, was greatly angered, rebuke showing on his face — when court envoys left he at once added insult.

units.zh: 會契丹回圖使喬榮北歸，侍衛親軍都指揮使景延廣謂榮曰：「先朝是契丹所立，嗣君乃中國自冊，稱孫可矣，稱臣未可。
units.en: When the Khitan envoy Qiao Rong was returning north, Palace Guard Commander Jing Yanguang told him, "Your court made our former emperor. This successor was enthroned by China itself. He may call himself your grandson, but not your subject.
units.literal: It happened that the Khitan returning-map envoy Qiao Rong was going north; the commander of the palace guard Jing Yanguang said to Rong: "The former dynasty was installed by the Khitan; the succeeding ruler was enthroned by China itself — to call him grandson is acceptable, to call him subject is not.

units.zh: 中國自有十萬口橫磨劍，要戰即來！」
units.en: China has a hundred thousand blades ready to grind you down. If you want war, come and get it!"
units.literal: China has its own hundred thousand mouths of swords honed crosswise — if you want war, come!"

units.zh: 榮至本國，具言其事，德光大怒，會青州楊光遠叛，遣使構之。
units.en: Rong reported every word at home. Deguang was enraged. When Yang Guangyuan rebelled in Qingzhou, Deguang sent envoys to encourage him.
units.literal: When Rong reached his own state he reported the matter in full; Deguang was greatly angered. It happened that Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou rebelled, and he sent envoys to incite him.

units.zh: 明年冬，德光率諸部南下，開運元年春，陷祁州，直抵大河，少帝幸澶州以禦之。
units.en: The next winter Deguang marched south with all his tribes. In the spring of Kaiyun 1 he took Qizhou and reached the Yellow River. The Young Emperor went to Chanzhou to meet him.
units.literal: The next winter Deguang led the tribes south; in the spring of Kaiyun 1 he took Qizhou, drove straight to the Great River; the Young Emperor went to Chanzhou to resist.

units.zh: 其年三月，德光敗於陽城，棄其車帳，乘一橐駝奔至幽州。
units.en: In the third month he was defeated at Yangcheng, abandoned his wagons and tents, and fled on a single camel to Youzhou.
units.literal: In the third month of that year Deguang was defeated at Yangcheng, abandoned his carts and tents, rode a single camel in flight to Youzhou.

units.zh: 因怒其失律，自大首領已下各杖數百，唯趙延壽免焉。
units.en: Furious at the disorder, he had every chief from the highest down flogged hundreds of times. Only Zhao Yanshou was spared.
units.literal: Angered at their breach of discipline, from the great chiefs downward each was flogged hundreds of strokes — only Zhao Yanshou was spared.

units.zh: 是時，契丹連歲入寇，晉氏疲於奔命，邊民被苦，幾無寧日，晉相桑維翰勸少帝求和於契丹，以紓國難，少帝許之，乃遣使奉表稱臣，卑辭首過。
units.en: The Khitan had raided year after year. The Jin court was exhausted, the border people knew no peace. Chancellor Sang Weihan urged the Young Emperor to sue for peace. He agreed and sent envoys with a humble memorial calling himself subject and confessing fault.
units.literal: At that time the Khitan invaded year after year; the Jin house was worn out running to and fro, frontier people suffered hardship, almost no day of peace — Jin Chancellor Sang Weihan urged the Young Emperor to seek peace with the Khitan to ease the state's peril; the Young Emperor agreed and sent envoys with a memorial calling himself subject, humble words confessing fault first.

units.zh: 使回，德光報曰：「但使桑維翰、景延廣自來，並割鎮、定與我，則可通和也。」
units.en: When the envoys returned, Deguang replied, "Peace is possible only if Sang Weihan and Jing Yanguang come in person and Zhen and Ding are ceded to me."
units.literal: When the envoys returned, Deguang replied: "Only if Sang Weihan and Jing Yanguang come in person, and moreover cede Zhen and Ding to me, then peace can be opened."

units.zh: 朝廷知其不可，乃止。
units.en: The court knew that was impossible and abandoned the effort.
units.literal: The court knew this was impossible and therefore stopped.

units.zh: 時契丹諸部頻年出征，蕃國君臣稍厭兵革，德光母嘗謂蕃漢臣僚曰：「南朝漢兒爭得一向臥耶！
units.en: Years of campaigning had wearied the Khitan court. Deguang's mother once told her officials, "Do those southern Han think they can just lie on their sides forever?
units.literal: At that time the Khitan tribes had campaigned year after year; the barbarian state's ruler and ministers gradually wearied of arms; Deguang's mother once said to barbarian and Han officials: "How can the southern Han brats just lie on their sides all the time!

units.zh: 自古及今，惟聞漢來和蕃，不聞蕃去和漢，待伊漢兒的當回心，則我亦不惜通好也。」
units.en: From antiquity to now it has always been the Han who sue for peace with us, not the other way around. When those Han come to their senses, I too will not refuse friendship."
units.literal: From antiquity to now one has only heard of Han coming to make peace with barbarians, not heard of barbarians going to make peace with Han — wait until those Han brats should turn their hearts, then I too will not begrudge opening friendly relations."

units.zh: 三年，樂壽監軍王巒繼有密奏，苦言瀛、鄚可取之狀。
units.en: In year three the Leshou supervisor Wang Luan sent repeated secret memorials insisting that Ying and Mo could be seized.
units.literal: In the third year the Leshou army supervisor Wang Luan repeatedly sent secret memorials bitterly stating how Ying and Mo could be taken.

units.zh: 十月，少帝遣杜重威、李守貞等率兵經略。
units.en: In the tenth month the Young Emperor sent Du Chongwei, Li Shouzhen, and others on campaign.
units.literal: In the tenth month the Young Emperor sent Du Chongwei, Li Shouzhen, and others to lead troops on campaign.

units.zh: 十一月，蕃將高牟翰敗晉師於瀛州之北，梁漢璋死之。
units.en: In the eleventh month the Khitan general Gao Mouhan routed the Jin army north of Yingzhou. Liang Hanzhang was killed.
units.literal: In the eleventh month the barbarian general Gao Mouhan defeated Jin troops north of Yingzhou; Liang Hanzhang died.

units.zh: 契丹主聞晉既出師，自率諸部由易、定抵鎮州，杜重威等自瀛州西趨常山，至中渡橋，敵已至矣，兩軍隔滹水而寨焉。
units.en: Hearing that the Jin had marched, the Khitan ruler led his tribes from Yi and Ding to Zhenzhou while Du Chongwei advanced west from Yingzhou toward Changshan. At Zhongdu Bridge the enemy was already there. The two armies camped on opposite banks of the Hutuo River.
units.literal: The Khitan lord, hearing the Jin had marched out, personally led the tribes from Yi and Ding to Zhenzhou; Du Chongwei and others from Yingzhou went west toward Changshan; reaching Zhongdu Bridge, the enemy had already arrived — the two armies camped facing each other across the Hutuo River.

units.zh: 十二月十日，杜重威率諸軍降於契丹，語在《晉少帝紀》中。
units.en: On the tenth day of the twelfth month Du Chongwei surrendered his entire army to the Khitan. The full account appears in the Basic Annals of the Jin Young Emperor.
units.literal: On the tenth day of the twelfth month Du Chongwei led all armies to surrender to the Khitan — the account is in the "Basic Annals of the Jin Young Emperor."

units.zh: 十二日，德光入鎮州，大犒將士。
units.en: On the twelfth day Deguang entered Zhenzhou and feasted his troops.
units.literal: On the twelfth day Deguang entered Zhenzhou and lavishly rewarded officers and soldiers.

units.zh: 十四日，自鎮州南行，中渡降軍所釋甲仗百萬計，並令於鎮州收貯，戰馬數萬匹，長驅而北。
units.en: On the fourteenth he marched south from Zhenzhou. The surrendered Jin army had abandoned arms in the millions, which he ordered stored at Zhenzhou, along with tens of thousands of horses. Then he drove north at speed.
units.literal: On the fourteenth day he went south from Zhenzhou; the surrendered troops at Zhongdu had cast off armor and weapons reckoned in the millions — all were ordered stored at Zhenzhou; war horses numbered in the tens of thousands; he drove north at speed.

units.zh: 命張彥澤領二千騎先趨東京，遣重威部轄降兵取邢、相路前進。
units.en: He sent Zhang Yanze ahead with two thousand horsemen toward the Eastern Capital and ordered Chongwei to lead the surrendered troops along the Xing and Xiang route.
units.literal: He ordered Zhang Yanze to lead two thousand horsemen in advance to rush to the Eastern Capital, and sent Chongwei to command the surrendered troops along the Xing and Xiang route forward.

units.zh: 晉少帝遣子延煦、延寶奉降表於契丹，並傳國寶一紐至牙帳。
units.en: The Young Emperor sent his sons Yanshu and Yanbao with the surrender memorial and the imperial seal cord to the Khitan camp.
units.literal: The Jin Young Emperor sent his sons Yanshu and Yanbao to present the surrender memorial to the Khitan, and also sent the dynastic treasure on one cord to the tent headquarters.

units.zh: 明年春正月朔日，德光至汴北，文武百官迎於路。
units.en: On New Year's Day of the following spring Deguang reached the north bank of Bian. Civil and military officials met him on the road.
units.literal: On the first day of the first month of the following spring Deguang reached north of Bian; civil and military officials welcomed him on the road.

units.zh: 是日入宮，至昏復出，次於赤崗。
units.en: That day he entered the palace but withdrew at dusk and camped at Chigang.
units.literal: That day he entered the palace; at dusk he came out again and halted at Chigang.

units.zh: 五日，宣制降晉少帝為負義侯，於黃龍府安置。
units.en: On the fifth day he demoted the Young Emperor to Marquis Who Betrayed Righteousness and sent him to Huanglong Prefecture.
units.literal: On the fifth day he proclaimed an edict demoting the Jin Young Emperor to Marquis Who Betrayed Righteousness, to be settled at Huanglong Prefecture.

units.zh: 七日，德光復自赤崗入居於大內，分命使臣於京城及往諸道括借錢帛。
units.en: On the seventh day he moved from Chigang into the inner palace and sent agents through the capital and every circuit to seize money and silk.
units.literal: On the seventh day Deguang again from Chigang entered and dwelt in the inner palace, separately ordering envoys in the capital and to the various circuits to levy and borrow money and silks.

units.zh: 偽命以李崧為西廳樞密使，以馮道為太傅，以左僕射和凝及北來翰林學士承旨張礪為宰相。
units.en: He appointed Li Song Grand Councilor of the Western Hall, Feng Dao Grand Tutor, and He Ning and the northern Hanlin academician Zhang Li as chancellors.
units.literal: He falsely appointed Li Song Western Hall Grand Councilor, Feng Dao Grand Tutor, Left Vice Director He Ning and the northern-arrival Hanlin academician recipient Zhang Li as chancellors.

units.zh: 二月朔日，德光服漢法服，坐崇元殿受蕃漢朝賀，宣制大赦天下，改晉國為大遼國。
units.en: On the first day of the second month Deguang wore Chinese court dress, took his seat in Chongyuan Hall to receive congratulations from Khitan and Han officials, proclaimed a general amnesty, and renamed the Jin realm Great Liao.
units.literal: On the first day of the second month Deguang wore Han court robes, sat in Chongyuan Hall receiving barbarian and Han court congratulations, proclaimed a general amnesty for all under Heaven, and changed the Jin state to the Great Liao state.

units.zh: 以趙延壽為大丞相，兼政事令，充樞密使兼中京留守。
units.en: He made Zhao Yanshou Grand Chancellor, Director of Affairs, Grand Councilor, and regent of the Central Capital.
units.literal: He appointed Zhao Yanshou Grand Chancellor, concurrently Director of Affairs, serving as Grand Councilor and concurrently Central Capital regent.

units.zh: 降東京為防禦州，尋復為宣武軍。
units.en: He reduced the Eastern Capital to a defense prefecture, then soon restored it as the Xuanwu command.
units.literal: He demoted the Eastern Capital to a defense prefecture, soon restored as Xuanwu Army.

units.zh: 十五日，漢高祖建號於晉陽，德光聞之，削奪漢祖官爵。
units.en: On the fifteenth day the Han founder proclaimed his reign at Jinyang. Deguang heard of it and stripped him of all titles.
units.literal: On the fifteenth day the Han Founder established his reign title at Jinyang; Deguang heard of it and stripped the Han ancestor of office and rank.

units.zh: 是月，晉州、潞州並歸河東。
units.en: That month Jin and Lu prefectures both went over to Hedong.
units.literal: That month Jin and Lu prefectures both returned to Hedong.

units.zh: 時盜賊所在群起，攻劫州郡，斷澶州浮梁。
units.en: Bandits rose everywhere, raided the prefectures, and destroyed the pontoon bridge at Chanzhou.
units.literal: At that time bandits rose everywhere in groups, attacked and plundered prefectures and commanderies, and cut the Chanzhou pontoon bridge.

units.zh: 契丹大恐，沿河諸藩鎮並以腹心鎮之。
units.en: The Khitan were terrified and posted trusted commanders along the river.
units.literal: The Khitan were greatly afraid; all military governors along the river garrisoned them with trusted men.

units.zh: 三月朔日，德光坐崇元殿，行入閣之禮，睹漢家儀法之盛，大悅。
units.en: On the first day of the third month he sat in Chongyuan Hall for the entering-the-pavilion ceremony. Delighted by the grandeur of Chinese court ritual, he was in high spirits.
units.literal: On the first day of the third month Deguang sat in Chongyuan Hall and performed the entering-the-pavilion rite; seeing the splendor of Han ritual and law, he was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 以其大將蕭翰為汴州節度使。
units.en: He appointed his general Xiao Han military governor of Bianzhou.
units.literal: He appointed his great general Xiao Han military governor of Bianzhou.

units.zh: 十七日，德光北還。
units.en: On the seventeenth day Deguang marched north.
units.literal: On the seventeenth day Deguang returned north.

units.zh: 發離東京，宿於赤岡，有大聲如雷，起於牙帳之下，契丹自黎陽濟河，次湯陰縣界，有一岡，土人謂之愁死岡，德光憩於其上，謂宣徽使高勛曰：「我在上國，以打圍食肉為樂，自及漢地，每每不快，我若得歸本土，死亦無恨。」
units.en: Leaving the Eastern Capital he camped at Chigang. Thunder sounded beneath his tent. The Khitan crossed the river at Liyang and halted in Tangyin county at a hill the locals called Sorrow-Death Mound. Resting there, Deguang told Palace Secretariat commissioner Gao Xun, "At home I took joy in the hunt and fresh meat. Since I came to Han lands I have known little pleasure. If I can reach my own country again, I will die content."
units.literal: Setting out from the Eastern Capital, he lodged at Chigang; a great sound like thunder rose beneath the tent headquarters. The Khitan crossed the river from Liyang, halted at the border of Tangyin county; there was a hillock the locals called Sorrow-Death Mound; Deguang rested upon it and said to the Palace Secretariat commissioner Gao Xun: "In my upper country I take joy in hunting and eating meat; since reaching Han lands I am often displeased — if I can return to my native soil, death will hold no regret."

units.zh: 勛退而謂人曰：「其語偷，殆將死矣。」
units.en: When Xun withdrew he told others, "His words were evasive. He is near death."
units.literal: Xun withdrew and said to others: "His words are furtive — he is probably about to die."

units.zh: 時賊帥梁暉據相州，德光親率諸部以攻之。
units.en: The bandit Liang Hui held Xiangzhou, and Deguang led his tribes against him in person.
units.literal: At that time the bandit chief Liang Hui held Xiangzhou; Deguang personally led the tribes to attack him.

units.zh: 四月四日，屠其城而去。
units.en: On the fourth day of the fourth month he massacred the city and marched on.
units.literal: On the fourth day of the fourth month he slaughtered the city and departed.

units.zh: 德光聞河陽軍亂，謂蕃漢臣僚曰：「我有三失：殺上國兵士，打草谷，一失也；
units.en: Hearing of the mutiny at Heyang, Deguang told his Khitan and Han officials, "I have committed three errors. I killed my own soldiers and let them plunder the countryside. That is the first.
units.literal: Deguang heard of the Heyang army mutiny and said to barbarian and Han officials: "I have three faults: killing soldiers of the upper country and raiding for fodder — the first fault;

units.zh: 天下括錢，二失也；
units.en: I seized money from the whole realm. That is the second.
units.literal: levying money throughout the realm — the second fault;

units.zh: 不尋遣節度使歸藩，三失也。」
units.en: I did not send the military governors back to their posts at once. That is the third."
units.literal: not promptly sending military governors back to their circuits — the third fault."

units.zh: 十六日，次於欒城縣殺虎林之側，時德光已得寒熱疾數日矣，命部人賫酒脯，禱於得疾之地。
units.en: On the sixteenth day he halted beside Tiger-Slaying Grove in Luancheng county. He had been feverish for days and ordered his men to offer wine and meat at the spot where he had fallen ill.
units.literal: On the sixteenth day he halted beside Tiger-Slaying Grove in Luancheng county; by then Deguang had had alternating chills and fever for several days and ordered tribesmen to carry wine and dried meat, praying at the place where he had fallen ill.

units.zh: 十八日晡時，有大星落於穹廬之前，若迸火而散，德光見之，西望而唾，連呼曰：「劉知遠滅，劉知遠滅！」
units.en: Late on the eighteenth day a great star fell before his tent like a burst of fire. Deguang looked west, spat, and cried again and again, "Liu Zhiyuan is finished! Liu Zhiyuan is finished!"
units.literal: At the si hour on the eighteenth day a great star fell before the domed tent, as if bursting fire and scattering; Deguang saw it, looked west and spat, crying repeatedly: "Liu Zhiyuan is destroyed, Liu Zhiyuan is destroyed!"

units.zh: 是月二十一日卒，時年四十六，主契丹凡二十二年。
units.en: He died on the twenty-first day of that month at the age of forty-six, having ruled the Khitan for twenty-two years.
units.literal: On the twenty-first day of that month he died, aged forty-six; he ruled the Khitan for twenty-two years in all.

units.zh: 契丹人破其屍，摘去腸胃，以鹽沃之，載而北去，漢人目之為「帝羓」焉。
units.en: The Khitan opened his body, removed the entrails, packed it in salt, and carried it north. The Han called it "the emperor's cured meat."
units.literal: The Khitan broke open his corpse, removed the entrails, poured salt upon it, and carried it north — Han people regarded it as "emperor's cured meat."

units.zh: 〈（案「以下原本闕佚」。
units.en: (Note: "The text below was originally missing from the received edition."
units.literal: (Note: "The text below was originally missing."

units.zh: 據《五代會要》云：四月十八日，德光卒於欒城。
units.en: According to the Essentials of the Five Dynasties, Deguang died at Luancheng on the eighteenth day of the fourth month.
units.literal: According to the "Essentials of the Five Dynasties" it says: on the eighteenth day of the fourth month Deguang died at Luancheng.

units.zh: 五月，宣遣制，以永康王襲位。
units.en: In the fifth month an edict proclaimed Prince Yongkang as successor.
units.literal: In the fifth month an edict was proclaimed appointing Prince Yongkang to succeed to the throne.

units.zh: 永康王者，東丹王之長子，以其月二十一日領部族歸國，改會同十年為天祿元年，自稱天授皇帝。
units.en: Prince Yongkang was the eldest son of the King of Eastern Dan. On the twenty-first day of that month he led the tribes home, proclaimed the Tianlu era in place of Huitong 10, and styled himself Emperor Heaven-Granted.
units.literal: Prince Yongkang was the eldest son of the King of Eastern Dan; on the twenty-first day of that month he led the tribes back to the state, changed Huitong 10 to Tianlu 1, and styled himself Emperor Heaven-Granted.

units.zh: 漢乾祐三年十一月，率騎數萬，陷邢州之內丘縣、深州之饒陽縣。
units.en: In the eleventh month of Han Ganyou 3 he led tens of thousands of horsemen and took Neiqiu in Xingzhou and Raoyang in Shenzhou.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of Han Ganyou 3 he led tens of thousands of horsemen and took Neiqiu county of Xingzhou and Raoyang county of Shenzhou.

units.zh: 周廣順元年正月，太祖命左千牛衛將軍朱憲往修和好，永康王亦遣使報命，獻良馬四匹，太祖復遣尚書左丞田敏、供奉官蔣光遂銜命往聘。
units.en: In the first month of Zhou Guangshun 1 the Zhou founder sent Left Thousand-Ox Guard general Zhu Xian to restore relations. Prince Yongkang replied with envoys and four fine horses. The founder then sent Secretariat Director Tian Min and palace attendant Jiang Guangsui on a formal mission.
units.literal: In the first month of Zhou Guangshun 1 the Founder ordered Left Thousand-Ox Guard general Zhu Xian to go restore friendly relations; Prince Yongkang also sent envoys in reply, presenting four fine horses; the Founder again sent Left Secretariat Director Tian Min and palace attendant Jiang Guangsui bearing credentials on a mission.

units.zh: 其年四月，田敏等回，永康王遣使獻碧玉金鍍銀裹鞍轡，並馬四十匹。
units.en: When Tian Min returned that fourth month, Prince Yongkang sent envoys with jade saddlery plated in gold and silver and forty horses.
units.literal: In the fourth month of that year Tian Min and the others returned; Prince Yongkang sent envoys presenting jade-and-gold, silver-plated saddle trappings, and forty horses besides.

units.zh: 其月，太祖又命左金吾將軍姚漢英、左神武將軍華光裔往使。
units.en: That same month the founder sent Left Golden Crow Guard general Yao Hanying and Left Divine Martial Guard general Hua Guangyi as envoys.
units.literal: That month the Founder again ordered Left Golden Crow Guard general Yao Hanying and Left Divine Martial Guard general Hua Guangyi on a mission.

units.zh: 其年九月，永康王為部下太寧王所弒，德光之子勒所部兵誅太寧王自立，稱應歷元年，號天順皇帝。
units.en: In the ninth month Prince Yongkang was murdered by his subordinate Prince Taining. Deguang's son Le killed Taining, seized the throne, proclaimed the Yingli era, and styled himself Emperor Heaven-Compliant.
units.literal: In the ninth month of that year Prince Yongkang was murdered by his subordinate Prince Taining; Deguang's son Le led his troops to execute Prince Taining and install himself, proclaiming Yingli 1 and styling himself Emperor Heaven-Compliant.

units.zh: 顯德元年春，太原劉崇將圖南寇，契丹將楊兗率騎萬餘以助之。
units.en: In the spring of Xiande 1 Liu Chong of Taiyuan prepared to invade the south, and the Khitan general Yang Yan led more than ten thousand horsemen to help him.
units.literal: In the spring of Xiande 1 Liu Chong of Taiyuan was about to scheme a southern raid; the Khitan general Yang Yan led more than ten thousand horsemen to assist him.

units.zh: 三月，世宗親征，與崇戰於潞州高平縣之南原，崇軍大敗，契丹眾棄甲而遁。
units.en: In the third month Emperor Shizong marched in person and met Chong on the southern plain of Gaoping in Luzhou. Chong's army was routed and the Khitan threw down their armor and fled.
units.literal: In the third month Emperor Shizong campaigned in person; he fought Chong on the southern plain of Gaoping county in Luzhou; Chong's army was greatly defeated, and the Khitan host cast off armor and fled.

units.zh: 二年三月，命許州節度使王彥超等築壘於李晏口，與契丹數千騎戰於安平縣，敗之。）〉
units.en: In the third month of the second year he ordered Xu Prefecture military governor Wang Yanchao and others to build fortifications at Li Yankou. They fought several thousand Khitan horsemen at Anping County and defeated them.
units.literal: In the third month of the second year he ordered Xu Prefecture military governor Wang Yanchao and others to build fortifications at Li Yankou; they fought several thousand Khitan horsemen at Anping County and defeated them.
